what_happened: Companion Verification task 233 (owner_labeled_agent_assisted_approvals) is already COMPLETED: approve.sh --via-prompt --assisted-by and check-approvals.sh's two independent checks are landed and tested, so the cross-repo prerequisite this task depends on is satisfied, not pending.

The research report had already settled placement, confidence vocabulary, artifact naming and the interaction design on cited evidence, so planning adopted four rulings as decided rather than re-litigating them; only the gitignore-pinning hazard and the refusal-predicate interfaces needed fresh derivation.

The obvious way to satisfy the 'deliberately tracked specs/certificates/' acceptance criterion -- adding a negation to the generated managed .gitignore block -- is a trap: that block's output is pinned byte-for-byte to a fenced block in orchestrator-runtime-files.md and is rendered into every consumer's specs/.gitignore. Plan routes around it with a lib header comment plus a mechanical check-ignore test case instead.

check-extension-docs.sh Rule E (check_referenced_scripts_declared) has no escape hatch for an extension that legitimately references an EXTERNAL, consumer-repo-owned script by name (approve.sh, check-approvals.sh live in the Logos/Verification repo's components/<name>/ dir, never in this agent-system). Rule E's exclusion sets (core_declared, all_declared_scripts, own_hooks) only cover scripts declared somewhere in THIS repo's manifests, so an external filename referenced in README.md/EXTENSION.md/skill/command docs always FAILs. Planned resolution: add a narrowly-scoped manifest field (e.g. external_scripts) to check-extension-docs.sh's exclusion logic in Phase 7, when skill-approve/SKILL.md and commands/approve.md first need to invoke approve.sh literally. Phases 1-3's own 'verify-deploy --only-gate 3,4 exits 0' bullets are therefore not literally achievable before Phase 7; the narrower explicit per-phase criterion (Rules A/H/Q/R/T/U clean) is used instead for phase closure through Phase 6.

Resolved the Rule E gap tracked since Phase 1 (approve.sh/check-approvals.sh are external consumer-repo scripts that can never be declared in any provides.scripts entry here) by adding a narrowly-scoped manifest-level external_scripts array field to check-extension-docs.sh's check_referenced_scripts_declared, parallel to its existing exclusion sets. Verified clean across all 23 extensions (no regression) and [approvals] now reports OK with no FAIL.

Phase 8's test-approve-classify.sh fixture surfaced a real parsing bug in approve-classify.sh: shape-based skipping of diff file-header lines ('---'/'+++' prefix match anywhere in the body) false-positives on a removed or added line-comment whose own content starts with '--', since a removed '-- comment' line renders in a unified diff as '--- comment' (diff marker + two-dash comment), indistinguishable by shape alone from a real '--- a/path' file header. Fixed by tracking whether the first '@@' hunk marker has been seen yet and only treating '---'/'+++'-shaped lines as skippable header lines BEFORE that point, matching how a real unified diff format actually disambiguates the two cases positionally.
